per_round:
The session focused on scheduler recurrence timestamp correctness and currency-rounding regression coverage, while the stated primary goal—replacing the hand-rolled retry loop in `ledgerly/sync/client.py` with Tenacity—has not yet been implemented.

For the scheduler, verified timezone resolution and DST behavior, added a regression test for UTC/New York wall-time scheduling across the April transition, and confirmed the focused scheduler/billing suites pass (31 tests). Ruff and whitespace checks passed. The full suite has 186 passed, 2 skipped, and one unrelated pre-existing invoice-rounding failure (`expected 1000, got 1001`).

Added `tests/test_currency_rounding.py` covering half-cent, negative, zero, small Decimal, default precision, and high-precision values; all focused tests pass, with `billing.currency` at 91% line coverage. No production rounding changes were made.

A production webhook v1-to-v2 cutover procedure was requested, but none of its ordered operational steps are shown as executed. It should be handled separately and cautiously, with authorization and production-safety checks confirmed.

The session added and validated extensive currency-rounding coverage, including precision scales, invalid negative places, mixed input types, and a large Decimal boundary. All six tests pass, Ruff is clean, and the full suite now passes: 184 passed, 2 skipped. No production currency logic changed.

Billing worker/consumer retention was investigated. `process_batch()` now removes an event only after successful persistence, preserving it on failure. `consume_usage_batch()` copies incoming batches before extending pending events, preventing shared-list aliasing. All 27 billing worker/usage consumer tests pass, including large sequential-batch regression tests. Memory tracing showed bounded behavior, though pending-event references should remain under review.

The primary Tenacity migration in `ledgerly/sync/client.py` remains unimplemented. A production webhook cutover began with a database backup table creation; all remaining cutover steps require caution and explicit production authorization. New secrets must use `vault://ledgerly/<ENV>/<KEY>`, and new Celery tasks require Locust proof of at least 400 successful executions/sec with zero timeouts. Keep commits small.

Billing worker memory retention was traced to `BillingWorker._last_batch`. Removing that unused reference fixed a new five-event isolation regression; 41 worker tests passed, a 5,000-batch trace peaked at 7.3 MiB and settled at 2.1 MiB with no pending events, and the full suite passed (118 passed, 7 skipped). `completed_batches` still retains full payload dictionaries and should remain under review.

CLI billing filters were refactored into shared helpers, preserving canonical `args.currency` and typed invoice-list behavior. Duplicate `--currency` declarations were removed, command assertions were modernized, fixture invocation succeeded, all 37 CLI/command tests passed, and Ruff is clean. Remaining argument groups are intentional global configuration, export format, and output mode.

The Tenacity migration remains unimplemented. Production webhook cutover requires explicit authorization and caution. Secrets must use `vault://ledgerly/<ENV>/<KEY>`; new Celery tasks require Locust proof of 400+ successful executions/sec with zero timeouts. Use sandbox host `https://sbx-pay-c.ledgerly.dev`; `sbx-pay-a` is retired. Keep commits small.

Billing worker memory isolation and CLI filter refactors are complete. Removing `_last_batch` fixed retention; 41 worker tests, trace checks, the full 118-test suite, 37 CLI tests, and Ruff passed. Shared CLI helpers preserve canonical argument names; an abbreviation regression test was added and passed, and stale comments were removed.

Work shifted to webhook delivery retries. `WebhookSender` now accepts validated `max_attempts` (default 3), retries transport errors and retryable server responses with bounded backoff, immediately propagates client errors, and re-raises after exhaustion. Added tests cover recovery, transport exhaustion, server-error recovery, non-retryable 4xx behavior, and existing success handling; all 8 webhook tests pass with sleep patched where needed.

The last full-suite run predates the server-retry fix and had one failure; rerun it before considering the work complete. Tenacity migration remains unimplemented. Production webhook cutover still requires explicit authorization and caution. Continue using the sandbox host, vault secret references, and small commits.

Webhook retry work is complete: lint passed, the full suite passed 44 tests, and the diff is clean. The Tenacity refactor was explicitly stopped until next sprint. A webhook deployment update to image `v2.8.1` succeeded.

Investigating search rebuild performance found sequential scanning, per-invoice embedding calls, and per-vector transactions. Rebuilder scans are now tenant-scoped, embeddings are concurrent and chunked, the management command shares its embedding client, and vector upserts are bulk-inserted. A 5,000-invoice dry run completed in 1.19 seconds with exactly 5,000 vectors. Relevant search, management-command, and storage tests pass after adding the required unique tenant/document migration and batch-aware mocks.
